previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with severe polyarticular joint pain involving both feet, ankles, right knee, and elbow, following a recent switch from colchicine to Uloric for gout management. She reported new paresthesias in her feet and was unable to bear weight. Initial labs showed elevated creatinine at 2.1, consistent with worsening kidney function. Imaging revealed degenerative changes but no acute fractures. Rheumatology consultation suggested possible calcium crystal disease rather than classic gout, given no prior confirmation of uric acid crystals. Treatment included restarting colchicine every other day, reducing Uloric to 80 mg daily, and initiating a six-day prednisone taper for inflammation. Gabapentin was added for neuropathic symptoms. During admission, she developed leukopenia, likely due to colchicine, and a left thumb paronychia, for which she was started on cephalexin. Her pain improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for nephrology and rheumatology. Her kidney function remained stable but elevated, suggesting a possible new baseline.

ACUTE ISSUES
============

# Abdominal pain and diarrhea: The patient presented with 
nonbloody diarrhea in the setting of nausea and episgastric 
pain. Given her remote history of C. difficile and 
immunosuppression, the patient was empirically started on PO 
vancomycin. When the stool PCR test returned negative, PO 
vancomycin was discontinued. As her diarrhea slowed, her diet 
was advanced to regular. As she remained afebrile and had no WBC 
count, her diarrhea could have been a viral gastroenteritits 
that took longer to recover from than usual (given her 
immunosuppression). Viral stool studies, ___ and ___ O+P 
(initial negative), and CMV VL are pending at discharge. 
However, the patient had persistent epigastric pain and nausea. 
She had a normal EGD in ___. A colonoscopy in ___ showed 
ulcers (result of moviprep versus inflammatory bowel disease). 
H. pylori was negative. As the differential included gastritis 
vs. PUD, GI was consulted to determine the need for an inpatient 
or outpatient scope. Famotidine was stopped and she was started 
on an empiric trial of pantoprazole 40mg BID. Her epigastric 
pain improved, and her nausea improved with zofran. GI 
recommended follow-up EGD as an outpatient. With improvement in 
her symptoms, she was discharged with scripts for pantoprazole 
40mg BID and zofran 4mg Q8H:PRN as well as follow-up with GI on 
___ at 2:30pm.

# UTI: The pt was noted to have some dysuria on ___. He UA 
was positive and she was started on CTX on ___ (PCN and FQ 
allergies). Her urine cx was preliminary positive for E. coli. 
She was transitioned to cefpodoxime 400mg PO Q12 for 3 days on 
discharge.

==============

patient presented with a Cr at baseline and no signs of 
rejection. Immunosuppression with tacrolimus and sirolimus was 
continued at previous doses, as levels of both drugs were

discharge. She has follow-up scheduled in transplant nephrology
